newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh says that he will release information detailing the process the government uses to approve the importation of logs from Cambodia. Thai logging has been the subject of criticism by non-governmental organisations, who claimed that the practice was responsible for the dwindling forests in Cambodia. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- The Counter Corruption Commission (CCC) is planning to establish an intelligence unit to monitor senior civil servants and top political officials as part of a new, pro-active working philisophy favoured by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. Late last year, the prime minister instructed the CCC to be more aggressive and focus its work on "big fish", and not petty fraud cases involving junior officials. (THE NATION)

- Thailand has postponed the signing of a contract to use a Canadian satellite to survey the country's natural resources. The decision was made on Tuesday as the prime minister ordered the cabinet to tighten budgetary spending on unnecessary or non-urgent projects. Canadian prime minister Jean Chretien is now on a state visit to Thailand. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Bank of Thailand (BOT) is drafting the terms of reference (TOR) on regulations and conditions for the merger of finance companies applying for the remaining two new bank licences. The TOR will require large finance firms to act as a core while smaller finance companies will be supported in the group. The central bank would make sure small finance companies with operational problems were involved in the mergers. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Italian-Thai Development Plc denies Philippine senate president Ernesto Maceda's claims that it has committed the "grandmother of all scams" in a land development project in Manila Bay. The company dismisses the allegations as merely a political ploy by an opposition party against the Philippine government. (BANGKOK POST)

- Deputy Interior Minister Pairote Lohsunthorn has proposed the government subsidise interest expenses on house purchases by local buyers rather than issue residence visas to foreigners, as part of its lifeline to the property market. His proposal runs counter to the plan announced earlier by the finance ministry to give a residence visa to any foreigner who spends a certain amount on property purchases in Thailand. The issue is expected to be discussed by the Cabinet next Tuesday. (THE NATION)
